newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Kodak Q1 hurt by strong U.S. dollar.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Kodak Q1 hurt by strong U.S. dollar.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co first quarter sales were hurt by the strength of the U.S. dollar, which ate into sales by about $90 million, Chief Financial Officer Harry Kavetas said on Tuesday.
Including the currency issues, sales were flat in January and February, but were up five percent in March, he said in an interview with Reuters.
Despite the lackluster sales in the first quarter, Kodak's stock rose about 2-1/4 in afternoon trading to 75-3/8 as analysts said the results were not as bad as expected.
Kavetas said he doubts the dollar will remain as strong. At current levels, he said the annualized effect on sales would be about $500 million.
"If the dollar stays as strong as it is right now...that exchange rate will continue to produce some pretty significant results," he said.

Kavetas said a "significant slowdown" in emerging markets continued in March. The company said that although sales in emerging markets were flat for the quarter, it continues to see that area as a source of long-term growth.

In the quarter, the company's sales of Ektacolor photo paper were its weak spot, shrinking between two and four percent worldwide and decreasing between 16 and 23 percent in the U.S. In areas outside the U.S., sales of Ektacolor rose between two and four percent.
An industry source familiar with Kodak said one reason Ektacolor sales dropped in the U.S. was because Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd won an account with Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
Overall camera sales rose between five and seven percent worldwide and increased between 24 and 31 percent in the U.S. In countries outside the U.S., camera sales were about even.
The company would not provide specific figures for its Advantix Photo System products.
Consumer imaging sales were $1.5 billion in the quarter, up three percent from a year ago, while commercial imaging sales were down 16 percent to $1.64 billion.
Kodak reported net earnings of $149 million, or $0.45 per share, on revenues of $3.2 billion in the quarter compared to net earnings of $274 million, or $0.80 per share, on revenues of $3.5 billion.

Excluding acquisition-related charges, the company's first quarter operating income was $272 million, or $0.80 per share. Analyst estimates were $0.81 per share for the quarter, according to First Call.
